extracted.intended_audience: pro se inventors and independent applicants preparing and filing USPTO patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for independent inventors on documenting an invention, evaluating patentability, performing prior-art searches, drafting the specification and claims, preparing drawings, filing with the USPTO, and responding to office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressman drafting approach (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasizes thorough invention documentation, careful prior art search, clear and detailed specification, and methodical claim drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat drafting as a multi-step process: document the invention well, evaluate patentability before drafting, search prior art to shape claim strategy, write a full specification that supports multiple claim scopes, and draft claims methodically to provide fallbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention documentation (inventor's notebook)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a bound, dated inventor's notebook. Record date of conception, description of the invention with sketches, modifications and improvements over time, tests and results, and witnesses' signatures and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a bound/numbered notebook to establish contemporaneous records and corroborate conception/reduction to practice; include sketches and iterative changes and have witnesses sign and date entries to strengthen evidentiary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability evaluation (pre-drafting checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before drafting, evaluate: Is it patentable subject matter? (process, machine, manufacture, composition); Is it useful?; Is it novel? (not in prior art); Is it non-obvious? (not obvious from combinations of prior art); Is it commercially viable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform these substantive checks early to avoid spending effort on non-patentable or commercially unsuitable ideas. Consider whether the invention fits statutory categories and whether novelty/non-obviousness are likely given known references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search (patentability search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a 'patentability search' before filing by searching patent databases, technical literature, products on the market, and trade shows. The closest art shapes claim strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough search informs whether the invention is novel/non-obvious and helps identify the closest references to distinguish over; use searches to tailor claim scope and anticipate likely examiner rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting the specification (required components and depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should: describe the technical field briefly; provide background sufficient to understand the invention; summarize the invention at a high level; describe the drawings; detail the invention with reference to drawings; and disclose multiple embodiments and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail to enable one skilled in the art to practice the invention and to support the breadth of the claims. Disclose variations and alternatives to preserve fallback claim support. Avoid minimal or vague backgrounds that fail to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting structure and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the structure: preamble, transition phrase, body. Use 'comprising' for open scope. Provide proper antecedent basis. Recite each element clearly. Draft 3-4 independent claims of varying scope and add dependent claims as fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formal claim structure and use open transition language ('comprising') to keep scope broad unless closed scope is intended. Ensure each term has antecedent introduced in the spec or earlier claims. Prepare multiple independent claims at differing scopes to increase chances of allowance and add dependent claims to preserve fallbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings compliance (USPTO rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should comply with USPTO rules: black ink, specific paper size, specific line weights, all elements labeled with reference numbers. Each figure should focus on a particular view or aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the USPTO formal drawing requirements exactly to avoid non-compliant submissions or requests to correct. Label all reference numerals consistently and make each figure clear and self-contained for the part it illustrates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing the application (procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: File electronically via Patent Center. Include all required components and pay the fees. Confirm receipt and docket all relevant deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit the complete application package (specification, claims, drawings, oath/declaration, transmittal forms, and fees). Use electronic filing, verify filing receipt, and calendar subsequent deadlines such as provisional-to-nonprovisional dates, priority claims, and maintenance of IDS obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to office actions (post-filing prosecution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most applications receive office actions. Read the office action carefully, identify each rejection and the grounds, pull the cited references and analyze them, decide whether to argue, amend, or both, respond within the deadline, and consider an examiner interview for complex issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address every rejection and ground raised, compare cited prior art to claim scope, and choose a response strategy (argument vs amendment) that balances preserving claim scope and obtaining allowance. Timely responses and examiner interviews can materially affect outcomes; consider counsel for complex rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common pro se pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent mistakes include: filing too thin a provisional; drafting claims in lay English instead of patent format; failing to do a thorough prior art search; over-disclosing in a way that creates 102/103 admissions; missing deadlines; and failing to file IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these anti-patterns by providing substantive disclosure in provisionals, using proper claim language and format, performing thorough searches, being careful what is admitted in the specification, docketing deadlines, and timely submitting information disclosure statements for known prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on hiring patent counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Even for a pro se approach, consult a patent attorney for complex inventions or for the office action response phase; the cost of professional help often exceeds DIY savings when the application is rejected on technical drafting grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limits of DIY filing: use counsel when claim drafting or prosecution issues are complex, when important commercial value is at stake, or when confronted with difficult office actions where technical legal arguments and sophisticated amendments are needed.
